svg.title: iPadOS · Import from device · pairing code · landscape
svg.desc: Mirrors App/ProjectTransferImportView.swift (enteringCode / connecting phases — pair, scanner) with App/PairingQR.swift, presented as a page sheet from CreateView. THE FIRST FILE IN THIS FOLDER, and it exists because this orientation is where the screen was wrong. Reported 2026-09-06: an iPad resting in landscape on a desk — the typical pose — showed the scanner's feed rotated a quarter turn and stretched across a slot four times wider than it was tall. Two faults, both only visible here. The preview connection was never rotated: AVCaptureVideoPreviewLayer's connection defaults to portrait and does not follow the device on its own, so the picture came up on its side. And the viewport was a full-width 170pt frame, which on this sheet is 552×170 — a 4:1 letterbox that resizeAspectFill filled by cropping most of the frame away. BOTH FIXED, and this file draws the fix: the viewport is now the shape of the picture, its aspect read from the camera's activeFormat rather than assumed (4:3 on every iPad — .photo preset, the widest view of the sensor there is and the easiest to land a code inside), transposed when the preview stands upright, and fitted inside a 340×250 box. So 333×250 here and 187.5×250 in portrait, centred in the column either way, on a sheet that is the same 580×640 in both orientations. Rotation now comes from the window scene, which is authoritative under rotation lock where the device is not, re-applied on window attach and on AVCaptureSessionDidStartRunning — the connection does not exist until the session's asynchronous configuration lands, so without that a sheet OPENED in landscape kept the portrait default until the iPad was turned. Verified on an iPad Air 13-inch (M3) 2026-09-06: the connection was found at portrait and set to landscapeRight, and the camera answered 4032×3024. THE CAMERA PICKER, bottom-trailing, 32pt on black at 50%, drawn only where there is more than one camera. That iPad has three — Back Camera, Front Camera, Front Ultra Wide Camera — so a tap flips front↔back, deliberately to the WIDE lens of that side so the flip does not land on Centre Stage's ultra wide, and touch-and-hold lists all three with a checkmark on the one in use. The choice is remembered across launches, the reason to make it rarely being a one-off. THE PAIRING ITSELF is unchanged and is drawn in full in iOS/library-import.code.portrait.svg: the scanner is a shortcut past TYPING, not past pairing, the payload is `LLXFER1:<code>` carrying the code alone, and a QR from another device fails locally against the pairingID hash before the network is touched. The Mac draws the same screen and decodes it differently — macOS/library-import.code.svg. Three states with no picture, desc-only, all on the same dark plate: no camera ("No camera available on this device." — what a simulator shows, which is why this file's geometry was measured on one and its rotation on a device), access refused, and THIS iPad shooting, where the viewport is replaced outright by one line. Geometry measured on an iPad (A16) simulator, 820×1180 pt, staged with LL_TRANSFER_PAIR=1.

g.text: Shown in Projects on iPhone 17 Pro, while sharing is on.
The code grants access to every project on that device, not just one.
Or scan the QR code shown beside it

svg.text: iPadOS · Import from device · pairing code + QR scanner · landscape · 1180×820 pt
mirrors App/ProjectTransferImportView.swift + App/PairingQR.swift — portrait is this sheet unchanged with a 187.5×250 viewport; the three no-picture states are desc-only
